title: HarvestWorks sensor-fusion onramp notes
content:
Context:
Met with HarvestWorks (HW) — industrial agritech startup building a real-time crop-health monitoring system. They aggregate multispectral camera frames + soil-moisture sensors + ultrasonic canopy-height readings at field-edge gateways. Goal: run an LLM-based anomaly summarizer + short diagnostic suggestions on the gateway and fall back to Redwood Private for heavy inference when connectivity is available.

High-level asks from HW:
- 200ms median end-to-end latency for summary on a gateway per 2s window (tight)
- Offline-first: must produce sensible degraded output when network is down for 30+ mins
- Keep PII/field-owner data on-prem; no uploads without explicit consent flags
- Predictable per-gateway cost across seasonal peaks; want options: Dedicated reserved or Private license

Attendees (recorded):
- HarvestWorks: Elena Park (CTO), Marcos Silva (Edge SW lead), Deepa Rao (SRE)
- Redwood: Priya Kapoor (SE), Luca Moreno (Applied ML), Samir Patel (Infra eng)

Raw call notes / fragments:
- Gateway hw: currently using Jetson Xavier NX + a small x86 aggregator (dual-core). Some 2nd-tier sites have Intel NUCs.
- Camera pipeline compresses to 640x360 multispectral frames every 2s; aggregated into proto payload ~180KB.
- Connectivity: LTE with frequent stalls (15–20% packet loss windows during storms).
- They run a lightweight CV model (edge) that emits a short JSON of detections. Want the LLM to consume 3–5 recent detection events + small metadata context and produce a 1–3 sentence diagnostic + confidence + 1–2 remediation steps.
- Elena: "If we can't match the latency goal we risk losing the operator UX. But accuracy can be slightly lower if the system is faster."

Proposed Redwood approach (brainstorm):
- Local inference path: quantized small-chat model (int8/4) running on Xavier NX using Redwood runtime compiled for ARM + continuous batching (batch window 50–100ms) to group gateway events.
- Prefix caching: maintain short KV cache of common plant-condition phrases per field to reduce generation length and cost. Cache warm-up on deployment and incremental updates from Private control plane.
- Fallback / degradation policy: when KV store unavailable or model swapped, return templated summary with core metrics (detection counts, humidity trend) and tag: "degraded":true.
- Async uplink: when LTE is good, stream minimal encoded conversation history to Private for re-scoring or longer-form summaries. Use zstd over HTTPS + per-customer KMS envelope encryption.

Gotchas / risks called out by HW / observed on call:
- Xavier NX has limited RAM; model must keep KV cache footprint < 12MB and working token cache small.
- Protobuf payload growth: their current detection JSON sometimes balloons to 2–3KB per event; need explicit schema pruning.
- Cold-start latency: first inference after gateway reboot is 2–3s (not acceptable). Need persistent process or fast warm loaders.
- Model size vs quality: they prefer operator-friendly phrasing. Small distilled chat models sometimes hallucinate remediation steps — need guardrails and eval prompt sets.
- Regulatory: some fields tied to cooperative agreements — data residency constraints plus audit logs for decisions.

Concrete requirements (capture for proposal):
1) Edge runtime: arm64-compatible Redwood runtime image, small-footprint model (<= 1.5GB quantized), persistent daemon to avoid cold starts.
2) Latency: 95th percentile < 400ms, target median < 200ms for per-window summary under normal LTE. Define fallback latencies for degraded mode.
3) Privacy: no raw images leave gateway unless flagged; only structured detection events and summaries allowed by default. Provide audit trail PID + signed attestations for uploaded events.
4) Cost: predictable per-gateway monthly for seasonal peaks. Provide options: reserved capacity + burst credits or private subscription with per-instance metering.
5) Ops: OTA model updates, rollbacks, and canary distribution across fleets of gateways.

Action items / next steps (owner, ETA):
- Luca: run a quick profiler for Xavier NX with two candidate quantized models (1.2GB int8, 700MB int4) and report memory + P95 latency. ETA 2024-11-15.
- Samir: prepare an arm64 runtime test image with minimal deps and a persistent loader to demo warm starts. ETA 2024-11-14.
- Priya (me): draft customer onramp one-pager (arch diagram + security checklist + cost options) and share with Elena. ETA 2024-11-13.
- Marcos (HW): produce a trimmed proto schema for detection events (max 10 fields, max 1KB/event) and share sample telem. ETA 2024-11-12 (they promised samples by EOD).
- Deepa (HW): confirm regulatory carve-outs for two Coop fields (need explicit audit log retention 2yrs). ETA 2024-11-18.

Prompt & eval notes (todo):
- Create small prompt set of 40 seed cases: common pests, irrigation misses, sensor drift, false-positive dust triggers. Evaluate for hallucinations and safe-fail behavior.
- Guardrail plan: response schema enforcement (must return JSON with keys: summary, confidence, remediation[]), validate server-side with strict schema; if fail, return "unable_to_classify" + metrics.

Billing / commercial notes (informal):
- HW is price-sensitive. We should surface two SKU lanes: 1) Private license + per-device monthly + premium for OTA; 2) Dedicated reserved fleet (commit for season) with lower per-device unit cost. They want numbers for 1k gateways seasonal vs 10k long-term.
- Ask sales to prepare a back-of-envelope for both lanes (avoid full contract until technical feasibility validated).

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Do we have a validated int4 runtime on Xavier NX? I think Luca's team has prototype for AArch64 but need to confirm kernel availability and kcache behavior.
- How aggressively can we prune generation length without losing operator useful context? Need AB test with users.
- Is there an existing Redwood audit-trail template we can reuse for Coop/regulatory needs? Ping compliance.

Meeting artifacts & links (copied for easy ref):
- Slack thread: #hw-onramp (link pinned in Elena invite)
- HW sample telemetry: s3://harvestworks-test/telemetry/2024-11-08/samples.tar.gz (they shared via pre-signed link)
- Demo ask: next call wants a 5–10 minute demo of warm-start local summary (Priya + Luca)

Immediate demo plan:
- Target: show 2 gateways (Xavier NX + Intel NUC) running local summarizer in warm mode, sample telemetry fed at 2s cadence, generation limited to 55 tokens, response schema enforced.
- Demo data: use HW trimmed proto (Marcos to share) or synthetic samples if not ready.

Communication draft for Elena (quick copy):
Hi Elena — thanks for the call. Following up with the proposed technical approach (edge quantized runtime + prefix caching + safe-fallback templates), action items and a short demo plan. We'll aim to have a warm-start demo by 11/14 and a profiling readout by 11/15. Will include an initial ops/security checklist for the Private deployment model.

Personal follow-ups (private notes):
- Prep two concise slides: 1) arch + failure modes, 2) commercial lanes with rough pricing ranges. Keep them simple for Elena (CTO).
- Remind Sales: emphasize seasonal reserved option vs pay-as-you-go to address their capex concerns.

End of notes.
